package.title: 100 Basic Electricity and DC Circuit MCQs for NAT-IE Practice

questions.question: A steady current of 2 A flows for 3 s. How much charge passes a point in the circuit?
A charge of 12 C passes a point in 4 s. What is the current?
In a metal wire, which statement correctly compares conventional current with electron motion?
choices: They move in the same direction

questions.question: A potential difference of 10 V transfers 20 J of energy. How much charge is transferred?
A resistor has 12 V across it and carries 3 A. What is its resistance?
What is the equivalent resistance of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 5 Ω resistors connected in series?
Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
A set of resistors is connected in parallel. Which statement about its equivalent resistance is generally correct for two or more positive resistances?
choices: It is greater than the largest resistance
It equals the sum of all resistances
It is less than the smallest branch resistance

questions.question: Three resistors are connected in series to a battery. What is the same through each resistor in the ideal steady-state circuit?
Two resistors are connected in parallel across an ideal 9 V source. What is the voltage across each resistor?
A device draws 2 A from a 12 V supply. What is its electrical power?
A 2 Ω resistor carries 3 A. How much power does it dissipate?
A 60 W lamp operates for 10 s. How much electrical energy does it use?
A 1 kW heater runs for 2 hours. How much energy does it use?
A 100 W appliance is rated for operation at 200 V. What is its operating current at that rating?
A 4 Ω resistor carries 2 A. What is the voltage across it?
For an ordinary metallic resistor, what usually happens to its resistance as its temperature rises?
Which expression relates the resistance R of a uniform wire to its resistivity ρ, length L, and cross-sectional area A?
A uniform wire is stretched to twice its original length without changing its material or volume. What happens to its resistance?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: Two wires have the same material and length. The second wire has twice the cross-sectional area of the first. How does its resistance compare?
choices: It is four times as large

questions.question: Which quantity is a property of a material rather than a particular wire’s dimensions?
In the circuit model, what does the electromotive force (emf) of a source represent?
A cell with emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω supplies 2 A. What is its terminal voltage while delivering current?
Two identical ideal cells, each with emf 1.5 V, are connected in series with the same orientation. What is their combined emf?
At a junction, 5 A enters while 2 A and 1 A leave in two branches. How much current must leave through a third branch?
A charge moves once around a closed loop in a steady circuit. What does Kirchhoff’s voltage law state about the signed potential changes around that loop?
choices: Their sum always equals the emf

questions.question: How should an ammeter be connected to measure the current through a resistor?
choices: Between two points without completing the circuit

questions.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the potential difference across a resistor?
choices: In series with the battery only

questions.question: What is a likely result of connecting an ideal voltage source directly across a wire of negligible resistance?
choices: A very large current may flow
The wire becomes an ideal voltmeter

questions.question: What does an open switch do in an otherwise simple DC circuit?
An ideal 10 V source is connected to a 20 Ω resistor. What current flows?
A 10 V source is connected across a series pair of 2 Ω and 3 Ω resistors. What is the voltage across the 2 Ω resistor?
Two parallel branches carry currents of 2 A and 3 A. What is the total current supplied to the parallel combination?
What is the equivalent resistance of two 4 Ω resistors connected in parallel?
What is the equivalent resistance of 2 Ω and 3 Ω resistors connected in parallel?
A 2 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel combination of 6 Ω and 3 Ω. What is the total resistance?
A 12 V source is connected across a 6 Ω resistor. What power does the resistor dissipate?
A 5 Ω resistor has 10 V across it. What power does it dissipate?
A 2 Ω resistor carries a current of 3 A. How much electrical energy does it dissipate in 2 s?
Two resistors of 2 Ω and 6 Ω are in series. How do their voltage drops compare?
choices: The 2 Ω resistor has three times the drop
The 6 Ω resistor has three times the drop
The 6 Ω resistor has six times the drop

questions.question: Three identical 3 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
Four identical 8 Ω resistors are connected in series. What is their equivalent resistance?
A 9 V battery is connected to a 3 Ω resistor. What current flows in the ideal circuit?
A 12 V source is connected to 4 Ω and 2 Ω resistors in series. What is the circuit current?
A 6 Ω resistor is connected across 12 V. What current passes through it?
A device is marked 100 W, 200 V. What is the resistance at its stated operating condition, assuming it behaves as a resistor?
A device operates at 120 V and draws 0.5 A. What is its power?
Two identical ideal lamps, each with resistance R, are connected in series to an ideal voltage source V. What voltage is across each lamp?
In an ideal current source circuit, what quantity does the source maintain at its specified value, within its operating limits?
A resistor obeys Ohm’s law at constant temperature. If the voltage across it doubles, what happens to the current?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: A 10 Ω resistor carries 2 A. What is the potential difference across it?
A 4 Ω resistor has 2 A through it. What is its power dissipation?
A 1.5 kW heater runs for 30 minutes. How much electrical energy does it use?
How many joules are in 1 kWh?
A 2 kΩ resistor is connected across 10 V. What current flows?
A 0.5 A current flows through a 20 Ω resistor. What is the voltage across it?
A 12 V source supplies 3 A to a load. What is the load’s power?
What is the SI unit of capacitance?
A capacitor stores 10 μC of charge at a potential difference of 5 V. What is its capacitance?
A 2 μF capacitor is connected across 5 V. What charge does it store?
Two capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in parallel. What is their total capacitance?
Two capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in series. What is their equivalent capacitance?
What usually happens to the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor when a dielectric material is inserted between its plates, with geometry unchanged?
choices: It remains unchanged in every case

questions.question: After a capacitor in a simple DC circuit has fully charged, how does an ideal capacitor behave for steady current?
choices: As a current source of infinite current

questions.question: What is the energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C at voltage V?
A 4 μF capacitor is charged to 10 V. How much energy does it store?
For a parallel-plate capacitor with plate area unchanged, what happens to capacitance if the plate separation increases?
choices: It increases in proportion to separation

questions.question: A capacitor stores 6 μC when connected across 3 V. What is its capacitance?
A 5 μF capacitor has a charge of 20 μC. What is the voltage across it?
Two identical 6 μF capacitors are connected in series. What is their equivalent capacitance?
Two identical 6 μF capacitors are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent capacitance?
What is the direction of the electric field at a point, by definition?
choices: The direction of force on a positive test charge
The direction of motion of an electron
The direction of conventional current in every circuit

questions.question: A uniform electric field of 200 V/m exists between parallel plates separated by 0.05 m. What is the potential difference between the plates?
How much work is needed to move 3 C of charge through a potential difference of 4 V?
How much work is done by the electric force when a charge moves along an equipotential surface?
choices: Equal to the charge in coulombs
Always equal to the source emf

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the charge of an electron?
choices: It changes sign in a circuit

questions.question: Why does a metal generally conduct electric current?
choices: It has no resistance at every temperature

questions.question: Why does a good electrical insulator usually carry little steady current under ordinary conditions?
choices: It has very few freely mobile charge carriers
Its resistance is always exactly zero
It produces an unlimited supply of electrons
Its voltage must always be zero

questions.question: An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. What is its net electric charge?
Two resistors in series have resistances R₁ and R₂. Which expression gives their equivalent resistance?
A battery is connected to a circuit with an open switch. In an ideal circuit, what current flows through the broken path?
choices: The same current as in a closed circuit

questions.question: A 12 V ideal source is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. What power is dissipated?
At a junction, 7 A enters and 4 A leaves through one branch. If there are no other incoming branches, how much current leaves through the remaining branch?
A closed circuit loop has a 9 V battery and two resistors with voltage drops of 4 V and 5 V. What is the algebraic total of the voltage changes around the loop?
Which property is desirable for an ideal ammeter?
choices: A resistance equal to the measured load

questions.question: Which property is desirable for an ideal voltmeter?
choices: Resistance that changes the measured voltage substantially

questions.question: A 3 Ω resistor and a 6 Ω resistor are connected in parallel across 12 V. What current flows through the 3 Ω branch?
A 3 Ω resistor and a 6 Ω resistor are connected in parallel across 12 V. What is the total source current?
A 2 Ω resistor is connected in series with a 4 Ω resistor across a 12 V source. What is the voltage across the 4 Ω resistor?
A 24 V source is connected across a 12 Ω resistor. What current flows?
A 24 V source is connected across a 12 Ω resistor. What power is dissipated?
A 2 Ω resistor and a 4 Ω resistor are connected in series to a 12 V source. What is the voltage drop across the 2 Ω resistor?
A wire’s resistance is 8 Ω. If its length is doubled while its material, temperature, and cross-sectional area stay unchanged, what is the new resistance?
Which is the SI unit of electric current?
Which is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
Which is the SI unit of electric charge?
Which is the SI unit of electrical power?
A charge of 1 C moves through a potential difference of 1 V. How much energy is transferred?
A source maintains a potential difference of 6 V across a 3 Ω resistor. What is the current?
A 5 Ω resistor carries 2 A. What is its voltage drop?
